meta.title: Compete. Build. Conquer.
meta.description: API Arena is a free competitive platform where students and developers ship real Spring Boot APIs as a ZIP, get them built in an isolated sandbox, and climb XP and ELO rankings. Submissions are scored out of 1000: up to 800 from HTTP tests and up to 200 from an AI review.

faq.a: API Arena is a free competitive platform for students, self-taught backend developers, and teachers. You choose a challenge, build a real Spring Boot REST API, and upload the project as a ZIP. An isolated sandbox builds and runs that API, then real HTTP tests score it. It is measured practice, not a slide-only course.

Each submission is scored out of 1000. Up to 800 points come from technical HTTP tests against the running API: functional correctness (300), performance (300), and REST design (200). Up to 200 points come from an AI review. The default review rubric is heuristic, and a language-model provider can be enabled per environment. XP tracks cumulative progress. ELO is a separate competitive rating that moves against the score expected for your rating and the challenge difficulty. Submitting again below your best score on that challenge is penalized.

Create a free account and open the challenge catalog. Read the public preview, then sign in and start a timed session to see the full requirements. Zip a Maven project with pom.xml at the archive root and upload it. The pipeline builds the project in a sandbox, calls the API over HTTP, saves the score, and updates the leaderboard. The docs hub explains the first submission step by step.

faq.q: What does a public challenge page show?
faq.a: A public challenge page is a preview only: title, description, difficulty, category, time limit, and XP reward. Endpoint lists, hidden tests, and hints are not on that page. They appear after you sign in and start a timed session.
API Arena is for students learning backend APIs, developers who want measured practice, and teachers who group students and review their submissions.

about.label: What is API Arena?
about.desc:
Build an API that solves the challenge. Submit your code.
Our system runs it in an isolated sandbox and <1>stress-tests it with automated checks, performance analysis, REST validation, and an AI review scored out of 200.

Your score enters the leaderboard. <2>In real time.
Improve, resubmit, and climb positions.
about.metricsExampleNote: Bars show point caps — not a sample grade. HTTP tests and code review are scored in separate blocks.
about.scoreReviewMode: Heuristic by default · LLM when configured

steps.desc: Browse challenges from Easy through Extreme. The public page is a preview. The API specification and hidden tests open when you start a timed session.
Ship a Spring Boot API today (more stacks coming soon). Dockerize it, zip your project, and upload it to the arena.
Your API runs in an isolated container. HTTP tests score functional behavior, performance, and REST design, up to 800 points. An AI review adds up to 200. XP and ELO update from that result.
Your score enters the leaderboard in real time. Analyze replay, iterate your API, resubmit, and climb positions.

features.label: Arsenal
features.aside: Multidimensional evaluation. It is not only whether your API works - it is how well it works.

items.title: Isolated Sandbox
items.desc: Docker-in-Docker. Your API runs in a fully isolated environment with CPU and RAM limits. No tricks, no shortcuts.

items.title: AI Review
items.desc: An AI review scores the submission out of 200, on top of the 800-point HTTP tests. The default rubric is heuristic; a language-model provider can be enabled per environment.

items.title: Replay System
items.desc: Replay every request, every response, every metric. Analyze where it failed step by step.

items.title: Multiplayer
items.desc: 1v1 real-time duels on the roadmap — same challenge, same clock, best score wins.

items.title: Real-Time Metrics
items.desc: Integrated InfluxDB + Grafana. P95/P99 response times, throughput, error rates, all while your API runs.

leaderboard.label: Competition
leaderboard.desc:
The leaderboard updates through WebSocket. Every incoming submission and every position change appears instantly, no refresh needed.

The ELO system ensures that climbing one spot in the top 10 matters more than dominating the top 100.
